eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent onshore flow and a strengthening marine layer have capped coastal heating at Los Angeles International Airport, keeping the official high near 82–84 °F on August 24 despite a broader Southern California heat wave. National Weather Service guidance and model consensus highlighted light westerly winds, partial stratus, and dew points in the mid-60s that suppressed daytime maxima, consistent with late-August climatology for the immediate coast. Trader consensus priced the 82–83 °F bin at essentially 100 % because any deviation would require rapid offshore flow or marine-layer erosion—developments not supported by the latest observations or short-range forecasts. A modest upward revision in the final NWS climate summary or a station-specific peak in the mid-80s remains the only realistic scenario that could shift resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from multiple models points to a daytime maximum of 25–26 °C under mostly clear skies and easterly winds of 10–20 km/h.** This aligns closely with the market’s top outcomes (25 °C at 54.5 %, 24 °C at 28 %, 26 °C at 16 %), which together capture over 98 % of trader probability.

Amsterdam’s temperate maritime climate normally produces late-August highs near 20–22 °C. Persistent above-average warmth this month (roughly +1.5 °C departure from the 18 °C August mean) and a stable high-pressure ridge have favored modest daytime heating. Easterly flow off the continent has reduced marine influence, lowered humidity, and limited cloud cover, allowing solar radiation to drive temperatures toward the upper end of seasonal norms. Official guidance from sources such as the Met Office and GFS-based products consistently shows afternoon peaks of 25–26 °C with negligible precipitation risk.

Model agreement on these conditions, combined with the absence of disruptive fronts or stronger winds, underpins the narrow distribution around 24–26 °C. Minor revisions in the final observational data or localized urban heat effects could still shift the exact recorded high, but current evidence strongly favors the 25 °C outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Panama City's peak temperature on August 25, 2026, centers on the narrow gap between 32°C and 33°C as the most probable outcomes, reflecting the typical range for peak afternoon readings in the capital during the wet season.**

Official forecasts from sources such as the Met Office and local networks project a daytime maximum near 31–32°C under partly cloudy skies with northwest winds around 10–15 km/h and humidity near 85–90%. Afternoon convection and scattered showers or thunderstorms—common in Panama's August climatology—introduce the main uncertainty, as earlier or more intense rain can cap temperatures by increasing cloud cover and evaporative cooling, while delayed or lighter activity allows brief spikes toward 33°C.

Model consensus shows limited spread in guidance, with historical analogs for late-August days in Panama City also clustering in this narrow band. Resolution will hinge on the exact timing and coverage of any convective cells relative to the daily maximum, typically occurring between 1–4 p.m. local time. Traders are weighting these short-term atmospheric variables heavily, producing the tight clustering around the two leading outcomes.

The close market split between 25°C (33.5%) and 26°C (34.5%) reflects model consensus on modest warming from Tuesday’s 24–25°C highs, tempered by increasing cloud cover that limits insolation and potential shower activity. A 27°C outcome (17.5%) remains plausible if clearer intervals allow stronger diurnal heating before storms develop, while lower probabilities for 24°C or below align with the risk of earlier or heavier rain suppressing temperatures. 

Key differentiating factors include the precise timing of any convective activity, urban heat island effects at measurement sites, and evolving model runs on steering flow from an approaching low-pressure system. Updated guidance closer to the period will likely refine these odds as observational data on cloud and moisture profiles improves.

eventMetadata.context_description: **A high-pressure system (wyż) dominating central Europe is driving trader sentiment toward 22–24°C as the most likely maximum temperature in Warsaw on August 26.** This setup favors mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies, light easterly or northeasterly winds, and dry conditions with minimal cloud cover or precipitation, allowing moderate daytime warming from overnight lows near 11–14°C. Official IMGW guidance and multiple numerical models (including GFS-based outputs) converge on highs of 22–25°C for central Poland, with Warsaw positioned between cooler northern air and warmer southern flows. Recent stabilization after earlier variable weather has reduced uncertainty, keeping probabilities tightly clustered around the 23°C (46%) and 22°C (32%) outcomes while assigning lower weight to outliers like 21°C or 25°C. Updated model runs and surface observations through August 25 continue to support this narrow range ahead of resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 26 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=mpmg

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from regional models indicate a typical wet-season pattern for Panama City, with afternoon convection and cloud cover likely capping daytime maxima near 30–32 °C. High humidity and the Intertropical Convergence Zone sustain scattered thunderstorms that enhance evaporative cooling and reduce solar heating, while any brief breaks in cloudiness could allow brief spikes toward 33 °C. These conditions align with August climatology, where average highs hover around 29–31 °C, producing tightly bunched market probabilities across the 30–32 °C outcomes as traders weigh subtle differences in model timing of rain and insolation. Updated guidance from local meteorological services will refine the range ahead of resolution.
